chunks: And by this chain of narration, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, who said: Zayd al-Shahham, Zurara, and Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to me from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), that he said:

If something flows from your penis of madhiy or wadiy, do not wash it, do not interrupt your prayer on its account, and do not invalidate your wudu on its account. That is merely like mucus (nukhama), and everything that comes out of you after wudu is from the channels (habail).

key_terms.النُّخَامَةِ: nukhama: phlegm or mucus from the throat; used as the legal analogy here, being neither najis nor a wudu-nullifier
key_terms.الْحَبَائِلِ: habail: the secondary channels or passages (as opposed to the primary urethral channel); fluids from these do not carry ritual consequences for wudu
key_terms.مَذْيٍ: madhiy: thin pre-seminal secretion during arousal; ruled ritually pure (tahir) in Shia fiqh, requiring neither washing nor renewal of wudu
key_terms.وَدْيٍ: wadiy: thick white discharge after urination; ruled ritually pure (tahir) in Shia fiqh, not a nullifier of wudu

ai.seo_question: Does madhiy (pre-seminal fluid) break wudu or require washing according to Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a ruling that madhiy (the light pre-seminal fluid discharged during arousal) and wadiy (the thick whitish discharge sometimes released after urination) are ritually pure (tahir): they do not require washing, do not nullify wudu, and do not necessitate interrupting salat. He reinforces this by analogy to throat mucus — itself neither najis nor a wudu-nullifier — and adds a jurisprudential principle that everything exiting after wudu from the secondary passages (habail) carries the same non-nullifying ruling.
